newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Indonesia's Suharto to visit Mandela, discuss Timor.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Suharto to visit Mandela, discuss Timor.

text.p: Indonesia's President Suharto will discuss East Timor with Nelson Mandela on a state visit to South Africa in November, Pretoria said on Friday.
A foreign ministry spokesman said Suharto would visit President Mandela from November 19 to 22 and the situation in Indonesian-controlled East Timor would be on the agenda.
"Yes, the situation in the region will be discussed," he said.
Mandela has asked Suharto to free jailed Timorese rebel leader Xanana Gusmao, who he was permitted to visit in jail on a visit to Indonesia in July.

Suharto ordered thousands of Indonesia troops to invade East Timor in 1975 after Portugal abandoned the colony in 1974. Jakarta annexed it in 1976, but the United Nations has never recognised Indonesian sovereignty over East Timor.
Human rights groups estimate that 200,000 people have died in the troubles, mostly through famine and disease.
Mandela's mediation could provide the "face-saving" device for Suharto to end the 22-year conflict, 1996 Nobel Peace Prize winner Jose Ramos Horta said on Wednesday in Australia.
Suharto, 76, has been president for almost 30 years and is expected to be re-elected unopposed in 1998.
